structure.title: Incubating strong growth
structure.summary: Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL), India's largest listed business incubator, incubates and divests businesses critical to India's growth. It has successfully built and demerged scalable businesses across ports, power transmission, thermal and renewable generation, city gas, and food FMCG, which now lead their sectors. AEL's vision is to be a world-class leader enriching lives. Its incubation model supports new businesses until self-sufficiency. Current focus includes new infrastructure and utility segments: green hydrogen, data centers, airports, and roads, which have significant long-term growth potential. These core infra incubating businesses contributed 60% to AEL's overall EBITDA in FY 2024-25.

structure.title: Robust business incubation model
key_items: Transport and Logistics; Services; Metals & Materials; Mining; Industrials
structure.summary: Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL) is the flagship incubator for the Adani Group, featuring a diversified portfolio across energy and utility (green hydrogen ecosystem, data centers, wastewater treatment), transport and logistics (airports, roads), primary industry (mining services, integrated resource management, metals, commercial mining, defence manufacturing), and direct-to-consumer (Adani One super app, NDTV). The document highlights a robust incubation model with proven success (APSEZ, APL, AESL in 2015; AGEL, ATGL in 2018), global recognition through rigorous certification (e.g., WINDGUARD for 5.2 MW WTG), significant shareholder value creation (31.2% CAGR over 30 years, USD 31.3 billion market cap), technology-backed operations (TopCon modules, OMCCC roads), efficient capital management (Net Debt/Equity 0.9x), and ESG governance (S&P/DJSI score 60/100 vs. sector average 29/100). It also covers capacity enhancement (4 GW cell/module, 2 GW ingot/wafer, 2.25 GW WTG, 5,000+ L-Kms roads), business models (B2B, B2C), and FY 2024-25 performance highlights including income, net worth, EBITDA, debt, PAT, total assets, CSR spend, renewable energy mix, and waste management.

nodes.title: Our Approach to Stakeholder Engagement
nodes.summary: Adani Enterprises emphasizes stakeholder engagement to achieve strategic objectives by embedding ESG principles and stakeholder expectations into organizational strategy. The approach is rooted in double materiality, assessing both the company's impact on environment and society and how environmental and social factors affect the business. A company-level stakeholder engagement policy, aligned with international and national best practices, guides engagement. The systematic approach uses an inclusive closed-loop methodology based on frameworks like AA1000 Stakeholder Engagement Standard, involving stakeholder identification, tailored engagement plans, and integration of concerns into policies and decisions. Continuous engagement includes periodic impact assessments, formal consultations, feedback, and grievance redressal mechanisms.

nodes.title: Pursuing a Clear Methodology
nodes.summary: The text outlines the company's stakeholder engagement methodology: prioritizing communication, feedback, and addressing concerns to shape materiality and corporate objectives. It details governance via a Board-level Stakeholders' Relationship Committee and an ESG Committee (CRC) of Independent Directors for quarterly reviews. It covers stakeholder identification and categorization, mapping on an influence/interest grid with tailored strategies, building a communication plan (content, objectives, channels), and using feedback mechanisms to continuously revise and adapt the engagement plan. It emphasizes co-creating solutions, trust, transparency, and mutual benefit for sustainable growth, and includes document identifiers (page 48-49, Adani Enterprises Limited Integrated Annual Report 2024-25) and section labels (Portfolio Overview, Corporate Overview, Strategic Review, ESG Overview, Statutory Reports, Financial Statements).

nodes.title: Our Approach to Materiality
nodes.summary: AEL's materiality assessment is a strategic tool reflecting core values and commitment to sustainable growth, aiming for a resilient, inclusive, and prosperous future through stakeholder engagement. The approach evaluates both the impact of operations on economy, environment, and society, and financial implications of ESG issues on business performance, integrating these perspectives for robust strategies. The double materiality assessment aligns with CSRD guidelines and incorporates GRI, SASB, and <IR> Framework insights for comprehensive coverage. It follows principles of double materiality: financial materiality (external environment's impact on value generation) and impact materiality (activities' impact on people, environment, and economy) over short, medium, and long term.

nodes.title: (Green Hydrogen Manufacturing Ecosystem)
nodes.summary: ANIL's WTG business enters its second year with a strong order book and stabilized production. Highlights include participation in Windergy 2024, a technology agreement with Windey, and commissioning of a German R&D center.

nodes.title: Outlook
nodes.summary: The Group is bidding on water infrastructure projects including wastewater treatment, irrigation, river interlinking, large-scale water supply, and desalination. Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) develops, operates, and manages airports with a vision to create world-class infrastructure and city-side developments, integrating modern facilities and technologies for enhanced passenger experience via Aviio and Adani One. AAHL manages seven airports, with Navi Mumbai as a new greenfield addition. It operates across eight city centres, controlling 50% of top domestic routes and handling about 23% of India's passenger traffic, serving ~200 million passengers. Airports are positioned as economic growth engines enhancing connectivity and employment, with a vision to be a world-class leader in sustainable infrastructure.

nodes.title: Segment Overview Introduction
nodes.summary: Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) aims to revolutionize Indian aviation with world-class passenger experiences, safety, and tech-enabled services, building integrated infrastructure. Its vision includes modernizing terminals, smart travel technologies, and sustainable practices to create world-class hubs driving economic growth. Product offerings redefine airports as vibrant commercial destinations using analytics and partnerships. India's aviation sector is poised for transformation with fleet expansion, airport doubling by 2030, airline mergers, record aircraft orders, and a young middle class, positioning it as a fast-growing global market.

nodes.summary: The text begins with the Adani Foundation's climate action focus, detailing community engagement for climate resilience through pond restoration, rainwater harvesting, check dams, bunds, and drip irrigation. It lists climate action thrust areas such as no barren area, sustainable water, waste disposal, plantation, sanitation, green energy, water conservation, and climate-resilient farming. It then describes the development of 400 hectares in Taranga Hills, Gujarat, in two phases using satellite surveys, drones, mechanised irrigation, and nutrient management for afforestation. Details about Taranga Hills' location, area, geography, flora, and fauna are provided. Plantation activities include ultra high-density planting, drone seeding of 65,000 seedballs and grass seeds, and integrated nutrient management. Water conservation efforts feature 11 ponds (4 lakh litres), drip irrigation saving 80% water, 65 check dams, 4 water tanks (2 lakh litres each), 16 borewells, and 280 rain guns. Biodiversity enhancement includes drinking water points, 22.26 km fencing, and zero tillage. Impact metrics show 400 ha total development, 3.0 crore litres rainwater harvesting capacity, 2.6 lakh trees planted, 2.5 crore litres annual groundwater recharge, 1.5 crore litres water storage sump, 0.5 lakh mandays since May 2023, and 50 ha developed in Phase I. Finally, a solar installation at BM Institute of Mental Health under 'Surya Ki Urja Se Sawarta Bharat' with 72 kWh capacity averting 80,640 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually is mentioned.

Conflict of Interest
The Code of Conduct strictly forbids the Directors and senior management from engaging in any situation that creates a direct or indirect conflict with the interests of the Company, such as activities that might lead to any undue gains or benefits for themselves or their relatives, partners, associates at the expense of the Company. Any Director found to have benefited unduly is required to reimburse the Company for the equivalent amount of the gain.

nodes.title: Rationale for identifying the risk / opportunity
nodes.summary: The text covers the rationale for identifying risks and opportunities related to business ethics and compliance. It highlights that ethics and integrity are foundational for regulatory compliance and stakeholder trust. Non-adherence can lead to legal penalties, financial losses, and reputational damage. AEL enforces a Code of Business Conduct and Ethics with training, audits, and zero tolerance, and promotes transparency and whistleblowing. Compliance is essential to avoid penalties and operational disruptions, and AEL uses robust frameworks, policy updates, audits, and training. The text also lists material issues: climate change adaptation and mitigation, and energy and emissions management, both as risks.

nodes.title: Rationale for identifying the risk / opportunity
nodes.summary: The text presents AEL's rationale for identifying climate-related risks and opportunities. It outlines negative implications: regulatory, physical, and reputational risks from climate change. AEL mitigates these by investing in clean technologies, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and expert engagement to ensure compliance and reduce environmental impact. It integrates climate risk management into business strategy to mitigate risks and leverage growth opportunities. The text also notes India's net-zero 2070 goal and potential financial burdens from stricter regulations. Additionally, it lists material issues: occupational health and safety, product/service quality and safety, circular economy and waste management, and human rights, indicating risk/opportunity status and financial implications.

nodes.title: Rationale for identifying the risk / opportunity
nodes.summary: The text covers AEL's material issues: safety, quality, waste, human rights, community engagement, customer satisfaction, innovation, biodiversity, water stewardship, and talent retention. For each, it indicates risk or opportunity, rationale, and mitigation approach. Safety involves training and hazard assessments; quality uses control processes and feedback; waste follows 3R and treatment investments; human rights include advisory forums and training; community engagement via Adani Foundation; customer satisfaction through quality and feedback; innovation via R&D and partnerships. Biodiversity, water, and talent sections are introduced but details are truncated.

nodes.title: Rationale for identifying the risk / opportunity
nodes.summary: The text outlines rationales for managing material issues: biodiversity (mitigating negative land use, compliance, reputation, TNFD alignment, stakeholder engagement), water management (optimizing use, reuse/recycling, stewardship policy, water-saving tech), and talent attraction/retention (competitive benefits, career development, engagement programs). It lists material issues 15-18 (Diversity, Equity and Inclusion; Learning and Development; Sustainable Supply Chain Management; Data Security and Customer Privacy), indicating risk or opportunity, and mentions financial implications and adaptation approaches for risks.

nodes.title: Rationale for identifying the risk / opportunity
nodes.summary: The text presents four risk/opportunity areas with rationale. First, DEI: promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion fosters positive culture and legal compliance, while lack of DEI risks reputational damage, legal challenges, and low morale; AEL ensures equal opportunities via policies, training, and monitoring. Second, employee learning: development enhances skills, productivity, and satisfaction, driving business success; AEL provides training, resources, and career growth. Third, supply chain sustainability: managing sustainability reduces risks and enhances brand equity; poor management causes disruptions and scrutiny; AEL integrates sustainability into supplier selection and monitoring. Fourth, data security and privacy: protection avoids legal issues and maintains trust; breaches cause financial and reputational harm; AEL implements robust measures, compliance, and cybersecurity training.

It outlines financial risk management objectives and policies, including market risk (commodity price, foreign currency, and interest rate risks) with sensitivity analyses, credit risk with expected credit loss movement and guarantees, and liquidity risk with contractual maturity tables. It also discusses capital management, including gearing ratio and compliance. Finally, it discloses derivative instruments and unhedged foreign currency exposures, and mentions contingent liabilities and commitments.

structure.title: A) Contingent Liabilities to the extent not provided for :
structure.summary: The text presents contingent liabilities not provided for, with comparative figures for March 31, 2025 and 2024, covering income tax, service tax, GST, VAT, sales tax, custom duty, excise duty, FERA/FEMA, stamp duty on demerger, and bank guarantees for subsidiaries/group companies. It notes a Supreme Court judgment on provident fund contributions with uncertain implications not currently recognized. It lists disputed claims and show cause notices under FEMA, Customs Act, Income Tax Act, and Finance Act with unascertainable liabilities, and a custom duty dispute on coal imports with amounts deposited under protest. Notes explain that most litigation is based on legal interpretation and management expects no material impact, other issues are ordinary course or not substantial, and future cash outflows depend on pending judgments.

structure.title: B) Capital and Other Commitments :
structure.summary: This section covers capital commitments, other commitments, legal proceedings, and lease accounting, including estimated contract amounts and lease liability movements. It details employee benefits, particularly defined benefit gratuity plans with actuarial assumptions, sensitivity analysis, and maturity profiles, as well as asset-liability matching and contributions. Related party disclosures list subsidiary, step-down subsidiary, jointly controlled, associate, and significant influence entities, along with key management personnel and non-executive directors. It also includes terms and conditions for related party transactions, loans, and other regulatory disclosures. Finally, it presents audit procedures, auditor responsibilities, and a qualified opinion on the consolidated financial statements.

nodes.title: Capital, Other Commitments, Legal Proceedings & Lease Accounting

Other commitments cover need-based support to subsidiaries and jointly controlled entities, with references to derivative and lease commitment notes. It details legal proceedings for dues recovery, pending at various stages, with management's provision assessment and reliance on General Reserve/Retained earnings. Lease accounting covers land and building leases with terms of 1 to 99 years and a 10% weighted average incremental borrowing rate, and includes a table on the movement in lease liabilities for both years.

nodes.title: Opening Balance
nodes.summary: The text presents financial statement notes for the year ended March 31, 2025, covering lease accounting and employee benefits. Lease accounting includes: opening and closing balances of lease liabilities, additions/deductions, finance costs, and payments; carrying value and depreciation of right-of-use assets (referenced to Note 3); expenses for short-term and low-value leases; total cash outflow for leases; maturity analysis of undiscounted lease liabilities (less than one year, one to five years, more than five years) and classification into current/non-current liabilities for 2025 and 2024. Employee benefits cover: defined contribution plan expenses (provident fund and superannuation); actuarial liability for compensated absences; defined benefit gratuity plan details including plan description, risks (investment, interest, longevity, salary), net expense recognized in P&L, net amount in OCI, balance sheet provision (present value of obligation, fair value of plan assets, surplus/deficit), changes in obligation and plan assets, plan asset categories (insurance policy), actuarial assumptions (discount rate, salary growth, mortality, attrition), sensitivity analysis, and maturity profile of gratuity obligations with weighted average duration.

nodes.title: Actuarial Assumptions, Sensitivity Analysis, and Maturity Profile of Obligations

It details the basis for the discount rate using government security yields. A sensitivity analysis shows the impact of changes in discount rate, salary growth, attrition, and mortality on the obligation for both years, noting that assumptions may be correlated. Finally, it provides the maturity profile of gratuity benefits, including the weighted average duration of 4 years and expected benefit payments across time buckets.

nodes.title: Asset-Liability Matching, Gratuity Contributions, Salary Assumptions, and Related Party Disclosures
nodes.summary: The page covers asset-liability matching strategies, noting the company's insurance policy for gratuity, a cash accumulation plan with yearly guaranteed interest, funding of deficits, and liquidity risk mitigation despite interest rate exposure due to shorter asset duration. It states the expected next-year fund contribution of ₹30.76 crore (prior year ₹22.27 crore). It explains that future salary increase estimates consider inflation, seniority, promotion, and market factors, and notes that insurer investment details are unavailable. Finally, it discloses related party transactions under Ind AS 24, identifying the controlling entity as Shantilal Bhudhermal Adani Family Trust (SBAFT).

nodes.title: Terms & Conditions for Related Party Transactions :

Other sections include common facility reimbursements, jointly controlled oil & gas blocks and termination notices, earnings per share calculations, CSR committee formation and spending, regulatory disclosures on loans, investments, guarantees, benami properties, wilful defaulter status, income surrenders, crypto transactions, and struck-off companies. It also addresses the short seller report and Supreme Court order, US DOJ/SEC indictment, segment reporting, proposed dividend, ratio analysis, audit trail, recent pronouncements, Social Security Code, subsequent events, and financial statement approval. nodes.title: Our audit procedures included, among others:
nodes.summary: The section details the audit procedures performed, covering litigation assessment, revenue recognition, and inventory measurement, including reliance on component auditors. It outlines responsibilities for other information, management's and the Board's responsibilities for consolidated financial statements, and the auditor's responsibilities, including risk assessment and communication with governance. Other matters include reliance on other auditors, unaudited joint ventures, going concern issues, and regulatory compliance under CARO 2020, with a qualified opinion noted. An annexure to the auditor's report is also referenced.

nodes.title: Our audit procedures included, among others: (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines audit procedures for three key areas: (1) litigation assessment, including evaluating management's evaluation, reviewing legal documents, using experts for provisions, and assessing Ind AS 37 compliance and disclosures, plus component auditors' work for NDTV and MIAL; (2) revenue recognition timing and adjustments, involving evaluation of accounting policies for variable consideration from coal quality variances, testing controls, sample transaction testing, contract review under Ind AS 115, and assessing management estimates and disclosures, with component auditor considerations for AWL Agri Business Limited; and (3) inventory measurement, covering evaluation of controls, expert competency, physical observation, and verification of book-physical differences for coal inventory.

nodes.title: Information other than Consolidated Financial Statements and Auditor's Report thereon
nodes.summary: The text outlines responsibilities for 'other information' in an audit context. Management and the Board are responsible for preparing other information, which includes management discussion and analysis, board's report with annexures, business responsibility and sustainability report, corporate governance, tax transparency report, and shareholder's information, excluding financial statements and audit reports. The auditor's opinion on Consolidated Financial Statements does not cover other information, and no assurance is provided. The auditor's responsibility is to read other information, compare it with financial statements of subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures audited by other auditors, and consider material inconsistencies or misstatements. Other information related to these entities is traced from audited financial statements or management certification. If material misstatement is concluded, the auditor must report; however, the auditor has nothing to report.

nodes.title: Management's and Board of Director's Responsibility for the Consolidated Financial Statements
nodes.summary: This text outlines management's and the Board of Directors' responsibilities for consolidated financial statements under Section 134(5) of the Act. It covers preparation and presentation to give a true and fair view of financial position, performance, cash flows, and equity changes in accordance with Indian Accounting Standards. Responsibilities include maintaining adequate accounting records, safeguarding assets, preventing fraud, selecting accounting policies, making reasonable judgments, and ensuring effective internal financial controls. It also includes assessing going concern ability, disclosing going concern matters, and overseeing the financial reporting process for the Group, associates, and jointly controlled entities.

nodes.title: Auditor's responsibilities for the audit of the Consolidated Financial Statements
nodes.summary: The auditor outlines objectives to obtain reasonable assurance that the Consolidated Financial Statements are free from material misstatement and to issue an opinion, noting reasonable assurance is not a guarantee. As part of the audit, they exercise professional judgment and skepticism, identify and assess risks of material misstatement, and obtain sufficient audit evidence. They assess internal financial controls, evaluate accounting policies and estimates, conclude on the going concern basis, and evaluate overall presentation and disclosures. They obtain audit evidence for group entities, noting responsibility of other auditors, remain responsible for their opinion, and describe responsibilities under Other Matters. They communicate with those charged with governance about the planned scope and timing of the audit, significant findings, deficiencies in internal control, independence compliance, and key audit matters.

nodes.title: Other Matters
nodes.summary: The text covers seven points: the inclusion of the Group's share in two unincorporated joint ventures based on unaudited, management-certified statements; reliance on audited financials of 166 subsidiaries, 22 jointly controlled entities, and 20 associates audited by other auditors; inclusion of unaudited financial information for 24 subsidiaries, 8 joint ventures, and 9 associates, deemed immaterial; conversion of foreign entities' financial statements from local GAAP to Indian GAAP; going concern assumptions for entities with continuous losses, suspended projects, and negative net current assets; emphasis of matter paragraphs by Navi Mumbai International Airport's auditor regarding disputed water development charges and an MCA investigation; and a jointly controlled entity's reporting under Section 143(5) with no adverse remarks.

nodes.title: Report on Other Legal and Regulatory Requirements
nodes.summary: This auditor's report covers statutory compliance under Section 143(3) of the Companies Act, including obtaining information, maintaining proper books, branch audit treatment, agreement of financial statements with books, and compliance with Indian Accounting Standards. It addresses director disqualifications, qualifications, internal financial controls, and Rule 11 matters: pending litigations, foreseeable losses, IEPF transfers, and fund flow representations regarding ultimate beneficiaries. It also covers dividend compliance under Section 123, audit trail (edit log) implementation and exceptions across entities, managerial remuneration under Section 197(16), and CARO 2020 reporting via Annexure A, with a qualified opinion noted in the Basis for Qualified Opinion paragraph.

Additionally, it outlines accounting policies for current/non-current classification, foreign currency translation, non-current assets held for sale, cash and cash equivalents, property, plant and equipment, investment properties, intangible assets, impairment of non-financial assets, and service concession arrangements, including financial assets/liabilities, derivatives, income taxes, inventory, provisions, revenue recognition, employee benefits, borrowing costs, leases, business combinations, and earnings per share.

nodes.title: a) Statement of Compliance
nodes.summary:
I. Basis of Preparation
a) Statement of Compliance
The consolidated financial statements of the Group have been prepared in accordance with Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) notified under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015, as amended from time to time and other accounting principles generally accepted in India. These consolidated financial statements have been prepared under the historical cost convention with the exception of certain assets and liabilities that are required to be carried at fair values by Ind AS. The Group's consolidated financial statements are presented in INR except when otherwise stated. All amounts have been rounded-off to the nearest crore, unless otherwise indicated and amounts less than ` 50,000/- have been presented as "0.00".

nodes.title: b) Principles of Consolidation
nodes.summary: The section on principles of consolidation covers the scope of consolidated statements, including the Company, subsidiaries, and equity-accounted associates/jointly controlled entities; the definition of control based on power, variable returns, and ability to affect returns, assessed through voting rights, contractual rights, potential voting rights, and relative holdings, with reassessment on changes. It details line-by-line consolidation with full elimination of intra-group transactions, balances, and unrealized gains/losses unless impairment evidence exists; presentation of non-controlling interests and attribution of OCI; equity transactions for ownership changes without loss of control; equity method for associates and jointly controlled entities, including initial cost, share of profits/losses and OCI, distribution reductions, elimination of unrealized gains/losses, discontinuing/resuming loss recognition, impairment, and fair value measurement of retained investment upon loss of significant influence or joint control; and recognition of direct rights and shares for joint operations. It also provides a comprehensive list of consolidated companies with details such as serial number, country of incorporation, name, relationship, and shareholding percentages as of March 31, 2025 and 2024 across jurisdictions, including notes on strike-offs, mergers, and classifications. Additionally, it addresses significant accounting judgements, estimates, and assumptions, reviewed regularly, covering estimation uncertainties for useful lives of property, plant, and equipment and intangible assets; impairment of non-financial assets; taxes, including provisions and deferred tax assets; fair value measurement of financial instruments; defined benefit plans; inventory measurement, especially bulk inventory at ports/yards; lease term and discount rate under Ind AS 116; asset retirement obligations; and recognition and measurement of contingent liabilities, provisions, and uncertain tax positions.

nodes.title: b) Principles of Consolidation (intro)
nodes.summary: The section covers consolidation principles: consolidated statements include the Company, subsidiaries, and equity-accounted associates/jointly controlled entities; control requires power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and ability to affect returns, with majority voting assessed alongside contractual rights, potential voting rights, and relative holdings; control is reassessed on changes, consolidation begins/ends with control, and uniform accounting policies and reporting dates are used. Subsidiaries are consolidated line-by-line with full elimination of intra-group transactions, balances, and unrealized gains/losses unless impairment evidence exists; non-controlling interests are presented separately, OCI attributed to parent and NCI, and ownership changes without loss of control treated as equity transactions. Associates and jointly controlled entities use the equity method, covering initial cost, share of post-acquisition profits/losses and OCI, distribution reductions, elimination of unrealized gains/losses, discontinuing and resuming loss recognition, impairment assessment, and fair value measurement of retained investment upon loss of significant influence or joint control. Unincorporated entities in the nature of joint operations recognize direct rights and shares of assets, liabilities, contingent liabilities, revenues, and expenses. A comprehensive list of consolidated companies and firms details serial number, country of incorporation, name, relationship, and shareholding percentages as of March 31, 2025 and 2024 across jurisdictions such as India, UAE, Singapore, Indonesia, Australia, and the USA, including notes on strike-offs, mergers, and classifications.

nodes.title: b) Principles of Consolidation (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines consolidation principles: consolidated statements include the Company, subsidiaries, and equity-accounted associates/jointly controlled entities. Control requires power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and ability to affect returns; majority voting presumption is assessed with contractual rights, potential voting rights, and relative holdings. Control is reassessed on changes; consolidation begins/ends with control, including acquired/disposed subsidiaries during the year. Uniform accounting policies and same reporting dates are used, with adjustments or additional financial information if needed. Subsidiaries are consolidated line-by-line with full elimination of intra-group transactions, balances, and unrealized gains (losses unless impairment evidence). Non-controlling interests are presented separately, with OCI attributed to parent and NCI; ownership changes without loss of control are equity transactions. Associates and jointly controlled entities use the equity method, recognizing initial cost, share of post-acquisition profits/losses and OCI, reducing carrying amount for distributions, eliminating unrealized gains/losses to the extent of interest, discontinuing loss recognition when share equals/exceeds interest (unless obligations/payments), resuming after unrecognized losses are recovered, assessing impairment, and measuring retained investment at fair value upon loss of significant influence or joint control.

nodes.title: Subsidiaries
nodes.summary: The text outlines the basis for preparing consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It covers the consolidation of subsidiaries when control is obtained and derecognition upon loss of control, using line-by-line consolidation. It details the elimination of intra-group transactions, balances, and unrealised gains/losses, with an exception for impairment evidence. It explains the treatment of non-controlling interests, including separate presentation, attribution of profit/loss and OCI, and handling of deficit balances. Finally, it addresses accounting for changes in ownership interests that do not result in loss of control as equity transactions, adjusting carrying amounts of group and non-controlling interests.

nodes.title: Associates and Jointly Controlled Entities - Equity Accounting
nodes.summary: This text defines associates and jointly controlled entities, explaining significant influence and joint control. It details the equity method of accounting, covering initial recognition at cost, adjustments for post-acquisition profits/losses and other comprehensive income, distribution reductions, elimination of unrealized gains/losses, and discontinuation of loss recognition when share of losses equals or exceeds interest. It also addresses impairment assessment and recognition, and measurement of retained investment at fair value upon loss of significant influence or joint control, with differences recognized in profit and loss.

nodes.title: Unincorporated Entities
nodes.summary: The text covers unincorporated entities in the nature of joint operations, detailing the Group's recognition of direct rights and share of assets, liabilities, contingent liabilities, revenues, and expenses, which are incorporated into financial statements. It then provides a comprehensive list of companies and firms included in consolidation, including their serial number, country of incorporation, name, relationship (subsidiary, associate, jointly controlled entity), and shareholding percentages as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. The list spans numerous jurisdictions such as India, UAE, Singapore, Indonesia, Australia, USA, and others, and includes notes on changes like strike-offs, mergers, and classifications.

nodes.title: c) Significant accounting judgements, accounting estimates and assumptions
nodes.summary: This text discusses significant accounting judgements, estimates, and assumptions in preparing consolidated financial statements, noting they are reviewed regularly. It details key sources of estimation uncertainty, including: useful lives of property, plant, and equipment and intangible assets; impairment of non-financial assets; taxes, including provisions and deferred tax assets; fair value measurement of financial instruments; defined benefit plans; inventory measurement, especially bulk inventory at ports/yards; determination of lease term and discount rate under Ind AS 116; asset retirement obligations; and recognition and measurement of contingent liabilities, provisions, and uncertain tax positions.

nodes.title: d) Current & Non-Current Classification
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: current/non-current classification of assets and liabilities based on operating cycle and Twelve-month criteria; foreign currency translation including functional currency, transactions, and group companies; non-current assets held for sale and discontinued operations criteria; cash and cash equivalents definition; property, plant and equipment recognition, measurement, depreciation (including oil & gas assets), exploration and evaluation assets, capital work in progress, and derecognition.

nodes.title: e) Investment Properties
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for investment properties, defined as assets held for long-term rental yields or capital appreciation. It details initial measurement at cost including transaction costs, subsequent measurement at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment, and the election to use previous GAAP carrying values as deemed cost at Ind AS transition (April 1, 2015). It also specifies depreciation over estimated useful lives per Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013, and derecognition/transfer criteria when disposed, used for own purposes, or permanently withdrawn with no future economic benefits, with differences between net disposal proceeds and carrying amount recognized in the Statement of Profit and Loss.

nodes.title: f) Intangible Assets
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for intangible assets: initial measurement at cost less amortisation/impairment; internal intangibles other than software not capitalised; mine development assets include land, overburden removal, and approvals; toll collection and airport operation rights capitalised per concession agreements; prior GAAP carrying values deemed cost at Ind AS transition. Finite-life assets are amortised over useful lives (software 3-5 years, mine assets over contract, toll rights 20 years, airport rights over operation agreement), with annual reviews and impairment assessments. Development expenditure is held under Intangible Assets under Development until project completion. Derecognition gains/losses are recognised in profit and loss.

nodes.title: g) Impairment of Non-Financial Assets
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Group's accounting policy for impairment of non-financial assets. It covers annual reviews of tangible and intangible assets for impairment indicators, estimation of recoverable amount, and use of cash-generating units (CGUs) when individual asset assessment isn't possible, including allocation of corporate assets. It defines recoverable amount as the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use, with value in use based on discounted future cash flows. It explains recognizing impairment losses in profit or loss when carrying amount exceeds recoverable amount, reviewing previously recognized losses for reversal, and reversing losses (except goodwill) up to the original carrying amount. Finally, it details goodwill impairment testing at the CGU level and prohibition of goodwill impairment reversals.

nodes.title: h) Service Concession Arrangements
nodes.summary: The section covers accounting policies for service concession arrangements, including revenue distinction and asset classification. It details financial assets (recognition, measurement, derecognition, impairment), financial liabilities (classification, effective interest method, derecognition), and derivative instruments with hedge accounting. It also addresses income taxes (current and deferred) and various other policies such as inventory valuation, provisions, revenue recognition, employee benefits, borrowing costs, leases, business combinations, earnings per share, and property, plant, and equipment movements, including concession asset transfers and no revaluation.

nodes.title: A) Financial Assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies from the notes to consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It details Service Concession Arrangements, distinguishing construction and operation/maintenance revenue, and classifying infrastructure as intangible or financial assets based on payment entitlements. Government Grants are recognized at fair value, deferred, and amortized to income. Financial Instruments are defined and classified into financial assets (trade receivables, cash, deposits, etc.) and liabilities (borrowings, lease liabilities, payables). It outlines initial recognition at fair value, subsequent measurement of financial assets under amortized cost, FVTOCI, and FVTPL, including business model assessment and SPPI criteria. Derecognition and impairment using the Expected Credit Loss model under the simplified approach are also covered.

nodes.title: B) Financial Liabilities
nodes.summary: The text covers financial liabilities, detailing their initial classification as either amortised cost or fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL). It explains the amortised cost category as most relevant to the Group, describing subsequent measurement using the effective interest rate (EIR) method, recognition of gains and losses in profit or loss, and inclusion of EIR amortisation as finance costs. It further defines the effective interest method and rate. For FVTPL, it notes inclusion of held-for-trading and designated liabilities, with fair value changes recognized in profit or loss. Finally, it addresses derecognition when obligations are discharged, cancelled, or expired, and accounting for exchanges or substantial modifications as extinguishments and new liability recognition.

nodes.title: C) Derivative financial instruments
nodes.summary: The text covers derivative financial instruments, including their initial recognition and subsequent measurement at fair value, with gains or losses recognized in profit or loss or OCI depending on hedge designation. It details hedge accounting, specifically cash flow hedges, outlining qualifying criteria such as economic relationship, hedge ratio, and credit risk dominance, along with documentation requirements. It explains accounting for effective and ineffective portions of cash flow hedges, discontinuation, and reclassification from OCI to profit or loss. Finally, it addresses income taxes, comprising current and deferred tax, recognized in profit or loss except when related to items in OCI or equity.

nodes.title: i) Current Income Tax
nodes.summary: The text outlines the accounting treatment for current income tax, including measurement based on taxable income per jurisdiction's tax laws, recognition of assets and liabilities at expected recoverable or payable amounts using enacted or substantively enacted rates. It specifies that tax related to items outside profit or loss is recognized in OCI or equity, addresses periodic evaluation of tax positions and provisioning for uncertain interpretations, and details offsetting of tax assets and liabilities when a legal right and intention to settle net exist.

nodes.title: ii) Deferred Tax
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: deferred tax recognition and measurement including MAT credit; inventory valuation at lower of cost or net realizable value with cost formulas; provisions, contingent liabilities and assets; revenue recognition for goods, services, service concessions, dividends, and interest, plus contract assets/liabilities; employee benefits including short-term, share-based payments, defined contribution and defined benefit plans; borrowing costs capitalization; lease accounting for lessee and lessor; business combinations using acquisition and pooling methods; earnings per share; service work in progress; overburden cost adjustment; and expenditure net of taxes. It also includes detailed tabular movements in property, plant, equipment, right-of-use assets, and intangible assets for two years, covering gross carrying value, accumulated depreciation, additions, deductions, foreign exchange, business combinations, impairment, and net carrying value, with notes on concession agreement asset transfer and no revaluation.

20. Instruments Entirely Equity in Nature (Contd.)
During the previous year, one of the subsidiary companies of the Group, Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) had issued Unsecured Perpetual Securities (“Securities”) of ` 2,624 crore. These securities are perpetual in nature with no maturity or redemption and are payable only at the option of AAHL. The distribution on these Securities are cumulative at the rate of 8% p.a. and at the discretion of AAHL. As these Securities are perpetual in nature and ranked senior only to the Equity Share Capital of AAHL and AAHL does not have any redemption obligation, these are considered to be in the nature of equity instruments.

structure.summary: The page covers three reserve-related topics within Other Equity. structure.title: e) Compulsory Convertible Debenture
structure.summary: The text details Compulsory Convertible Debentures (CCDs) issued by Adani Road Transport Limited and Adani Airport Holdings Limited. For Adani Road Transport, CCDs of ₹1154.95 crore are compulsorily convertible after 5 to 10 years from issue, carry 6.5% p.a. interest, and convert at the higher of fair market value on conversion or issue date. For Adani Airport Holdings, 19,95,50,734 CCDs issued in FY 21-22 have a borrowing component of ₹762.43 crore and equity component of ₹1,117.12 crore, are compulsorily convertible at par after 20 years, and carry interest at 6-month LIBOR+400 bps, later changed to SBI MCLR+100 bps from July 1, 2023, reset annually. Interest accrues annually; at maturity, CCDs convert to equity shares based on fair market value at issue date. The fair value of the financial liability is determined using a similar standalone debt instrument, with the equity component as the residual amount.

It outlines financial risk management objectives under Board-approved governance, addressing market risk (commodity price risk from coal and materials, mitigated by sourcing diversification; foreign currency exchange risk managed via derivatives with sensitivity analysis on profit before tax), interest rate risk (variable rate borrowings, central treasury oversight, 50 bps sensitivity), credit risk (controls, diversified receivables, expected credit loss allowances, corporate guarantees), liquidity risk (cash flow forecasting, contractual maturity analysis), and capital management (gearing ratio, net debt, total equity, return on capital monitoring, no external capital requirements, no covenant breaches, no policy changes).

nodes.title: 40 Financial Instruments And Risk Review (intro)
nodes.summary: This note covers the accounting classification and fair value hierarchy of financial instruments, detailing financial assets (loans, receivables, cash, investments) and liabilities (borrowings, payables) by category (FVTPL, FVTOCI, amortised cost) and fair value hierarchy levels (Level 1, 2, 3) for March 31, 2025 and 2024. It explains the three hierarchy levels and provides tables summarizing carrying amounts. It also outlines financial risk management objectives, covering market risk (commodity price risk and foreign currency exchange risk), including risk mitigation strategies and a sensitivity analysis of exchange rate fluctuations on profit before tax.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments, Risk Management, Commodity and Currency Risks
nodes.summary: The page covers fair value measurement of derivatives and FVTOCI investments using market observable inputs. It outlines the Group's financial risk management objectives and policies under Board-approved governance, addressing market, credit, and liquidity risks. Market risk is detailed as commodity price risk from coal and other materials, mitigated by sourcing diversification and procurement strategies, and foreign currency exchange risk from international operations, managed via derivatives like forwards and options. It notes open positions reference Note 41 and provides a sensitivity table showing the impact of rupee-dollar exchange rate changes on consolidated profit before tax for 2025 and 2024.

nodes.title: C. Interest Risk :
nodes.summary: The text covers financial risk management disclosures: interest rate risk (exposure from variable rate borrowings, central treasury oversight, 50 bps sensitivity analysis on profit before tax, and variable cost borrowings amounts), credit risk (definition, financial instruments affected, controls, diversified receivables including public sector units, movement in expected credit loss allowances on trade receivables, and corporate guarantees), liquidity risk (definition, objective, cash flow forecasting, and contractual maturity analysis of financial liabilities across time buckets), and capital management (objective, gearing ratio calculation, net debt, total equity, gearing ratio percentages, return on capital monitoring, no external capital requirements, no covenant breaches, and no changes in capital management policies).

structure.title: 41 Disclosure Regarding Derivative Instruments and Unhedged Exposure:
structure.summary: This disclosure details derivative instruments and unhedged exposures as of March 31, 2025, and 2024. It includes outstanding commodity and foreign currency derivative contracts, showing fair values for commodity hedges (copper, gold, silver) with price risk components. It presents notional amounts, strike rates, and gains/losses for commodity forwards/futures, and adjustments to inventory carrying values from fair value hedges. Additionally, it lists total foreign currency exposures hedged or covered by derivatives, including foreign letters of credit, loans, payables, and receivables in various currencies.

structure.title: 41. Disclosure Regarding Derivative Instruments and Unhedged Exposure: (Contd.)
structure.summary: This section of the Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, provides a disclosure regarding derivative instruments and unhedged foreign currency exposure. It presents tables showing total foreign currency exposures not covered by derivative instruments as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, categorized by type (e.g., Foreign Letter of Credit/Buyers Credit, Foreign Currency Loan, Other Payables, Others, Trade Payables, Trade Receivables, EEFC Accounts/Cash & Cash Equivalents, Other Receivables) and currency (USD, SGD, GBP, EUR, AUD, etc.), with amounts in foreign currency and Indian Rupees. Footnotes indicate amounts below 50,000 as '*' and provide exchange rates used for conversion as of both dates.

structure.title: 42. Discontinued Operations and Assets held for Sale
key_items: 42. Discontinued Operations and Assets held for Sale (Contd.)
structure.summary: The text details discontinued operations and assets held for sale under Ind AS 105. It covers the Parent Company's sale of its Power Trading business to Powerpulse Trading Solutions Limited for ₹8.50 crore effective December 24, 2024, and the subsidiary MP Natural Resources Private Limited's transfer of coal block rights and obligations to Mahan Energen Limited effective November 11, 2024. It includes a table showing major classes of assets and liabilities classified as held for sale as at March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, with amounts in ₹ crore for both businesses and totals.

It covers asset sales: NDTV's investment properties held for sale (₹18.58 crore), MSPVL's manufacturing upgrade and asset write-down (₹309.41 crore prior year, ₹88 crore current), and QBML Media's TV division shutdown and asset sale. It also lists related parties under Ind AS 24: controlling entity (SBAFT), jointly controlled entities, associates, key management personnel, and non-executive directors, with effective dates.

nodes.title: (F) Entities over which (A) or (D) above have significant influence with whom transactions have taken place: (intro)
nodes.summary: This section of the Consolidated Financial Statements notes (Note 43 contd.) lists entities over which the company or its subsidiaries have significant influence and with which transactions have taken place. It provides a numbered list of 165 related parties, including subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures, and other affiliates, spanning sectors such as ports, logistics, energy, mining, real estate, education, healthcare, and finance. The list includes entities like Adani Ports, Adani Power, Adani Green Energy, Ambuja Cements, ACC Ltd., and various renewable energy and infrastructure firms. It also includes foundations, hospitals, and universities, as well as international entities. The note concludes with a reference to a merged entity effective April 4, 2025.

nodes.title: Nature and Volume of Transaction with Related Parties
nodes.summary: This section discloses Adani Enterprises Limited's related party transactions exceeding 10% of each type for March 31, 2025 and 2024, covering four related party categories: Jointly Controlled Entities, Associates, Key Management Personnel & Non-Executive Directors, and Other Related Parties. It details 33 transaction types including sale/purchase of goods and assets, services, interest, rent, dividends, donations, remuneration, commissions, borrowings, loans, investments, perpetual securities, guarantees, deposits, capital contributions, and scrap sales, all in crore rupees. It also presents closing balances exceeding 10% of total balances for various balance sheet items such as loans, receivables, payables, borrowings, financial assets/liabilities, debentures, perpetual securities, and guarantees, with a footnote on Adani Power Ltd. post-amalgamation. Additionally, Segment Reporting under Ind AS 108 details operating segments (Integrated Mining, Mining Services, Commercial Mining, New Energy Ecosystem, Road, Airport, Others) with financial data on revenue, profit, assets, liabilities, investments, and capital expenditure, plus geographical segment information for revenue and non-current assets within and outside India, along with notes on discontinued operations and a prior-year segment reclassification.

nodes.title: Nature and Volume of Transaction with Related Parties (intro)
nodes.summary: This section discloses related party transactions for Adani Enterprises Limited exceeding 10% of each type, covering four related party categories: Jointly Controlled Entities, Associates, Key Management Personnel & Non-Executive Directors, and Other Related Parties, for March 31, 2025 and 2024. It details 33 transaction types including sale/purchase of goods and assets, services, interest, rent, dividends, donations, remuneration, commissions, borrowings, loans, investments, perpetual securities, guarantees, deposits, capital contributions, and scrap sales, all in crore rupees. nodes.title: ii) Nature and Volume of Transaction with Related Parties
nodes.summary: The text discloses related party transactions exceeding 10% of each type for Adani Enterprises Limited, covering Jointly Controlled Entities, Associates, Key Management Personnel & Non-Executive Directors, and Other Related Parties for March 31, 2025 and 2024. It details 33 transaction types: sale/purchase of goods; rendering/availing of services; interest income/expense; rent income/expense; dividend income; donation; discounts on prompt payment; remuneration (short-term, post-employment, other long-term); commission and sitting fees to non-executive directors; purchase/sale of assets/business; borrowings taken/repaid; loans given/received back; purchase/sale of investments; transfer of employee liabilities/loans; issuance of perpetual securities; release of corporate guarantees; security deposits given/received; contribution to partners capital; and sale of scrap. All values are in crore rupees.

nodes.title: iii) Closing Balances with Related Parties
nodes.summary: This note discloses closing balances with related parties exceeding 10% of total balances for each type, with amounts in crore and balances below ₹50,000 shown as 0.00. It covers multiple balance sheet items across four related party categories: Key Management Personnel & Non-Executive Directors, Jointly Controlled Entities, Other Related Parties, and Associates, comparing March 31, 2025 and 2024. Items include Non-Current Loans, Current Loans, Trade Receivables, Trade Payables, Current and Non-Current Borrowings, Other Current Assets, Other Current Liabilities, Other Non-Current Financial Assets, Other Non-Current Assets, Compulsory Convertible Debentures, Other Current Financial Assets, Other Current Financial Liabilities, Borrowing Perpetual Securities, and Guarantee & Collateral Securities. Specific entities and amounts are listed, with a footnote explaining Adani Power Ltd. balances post-amalgamation.

nodes.title: Terms & Conditions for Related Party Transactions :
nodes.summary: The text covers Terms & Conditions for Related Party Transactions, noting they are shown net of taxes, include discontinued operations, and are with parties in the ordinary course of business. It then presents Segment Reporting under Ind AS 108, detailing operating segments (Integrated Mining, Mining Services, Commercial Mining, New Energy Ecosystem, Road, Airport, Others) with financial data on revenue, profit, assets, liabilities, investments, and capital expenditure. It also provides geographical segment information for revenue and non-current assets within and outside India, along with notes on discontinued operations and a prior-year segment reclassification.

structure.title: 45. Business Combinations during the year
structure.summary: These consolidated financial statement notes cover: business combinations during FY2025 (Stark Enterprises, Quintillion Business Media, IANS India, Semolina Kitchens, Aviserve Facilities, Aviground Facilities, Cococart Ventures) with provisional fair values, capital reserve, goodwill, and purchase consideration; CGU impairment assessment under Ind AS 36; Adani Mining's Deed of Novation and amortization of deferred reimbursement; Navi Mumbai International Airport's concession agreement, disputed water development charges, and MCA investigation; pending CBI, Enforcement Directorate, and MCA investigations against Mumbai International Airport; approved schemes of amalgamation for Adani Cementation, Adani Green Technology, Adani Emerging Business, Adani Tradecom, Adani New Industries, and Stratatech Mineral Resources; the short seller report and related SEBI proceedings; and a US DOJ indictment and SEC complaint against an executive director.

structure.title: 48. Service Concession Arrangements
structure.summary: The text details Service Concession Arrangements (SCAs) between subsidiary companies of the Group and government authorities for road and sewage treatment plant projects. It lists 16 subsidiaries (a-p) with project specifics: location, scope, construction and operation periods, concession terms, project costs, and bonus conditions. It also outlines payment structures, including installments, interest rates, and bonuses. Projects include roads in Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Bihar, with costs ranging from ₹274.20 crore to ₹1,838.10 crore. Payment terms involve 40% during construction and the remainder in installments post-COD with interest.

structure.title: 49. Contingent Liabilities and Commitments
structure.summary: The text presents Note 49 on Contingent Liabilities and Commitments from the consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It includes a table of contingent liabilities not provided for, covering claims against the Group, income tax, service tax, GST/VAT/sales tax, custom duty, excise duty/drawback, FERA/FEMA, concession levy, and bank guarantees, with amounts as of March 31, 2025 and 2024. It notes a Supreme Court judgment on provident fund contributions with uncertain implications not currently recognized. It also lists disputed claims/show cause notices not considered contingent liabilities, including those under FEMA, Customs Act, Income Tax Act, and DGCEI, with unascertainable liabilities. Finally, it details a custom duty dispute on coal imports, including show cause notices of ₹863.62 crore and deposits of ₹460.61 crore under protest.

structure.title: 49. Contingent Liabilities and Commitments (Contd.)
key_items: ii) EPC 1080 Royalty; iii) Export Obligations
structure.summary: The text covers contingent liabilities and commitments from Adani Enterprises' 2024-25 consolidated financial statements. It details Mumbai International Airport's challenge of a MoCA order on Passenger Service Fees, an arbitration award excusing annual fees to AAI, and recognized expenses. It also includes capital commitments, royalty agreements for EPC 1690 and EPC 1080, and export obligations under EPCG and Advance License schemes for subsidiaries like Mundra Solar, Adani New Industries, and Kutch Copper, along with financial support to joint ventures.

structure.title: 50. Lease Accounting
structure.summary: This section covers lease accounting, including the movement in lease liabilities with opening/closing balances, additions, finance costs, payments, and forex adjustments for 2025 and 2024, plus a note on rail infrastructure assets. It also details right-of-use carrying value and depreciation, expenses for short-term/low-value leases, total cash outflow, and maturity analysis of lease liabilities with undiscounted cash flows and current/non-current balances. Employee benefits are addressed: defined contribution plan expenses, compensated absences liability, and defined benefit gratuity plan disclosures covering net expense in profit & loss and OCI, balance sheet recognition, reconciliations of obligation and plan assets, actuarial assumptions, sensitivity analysis, maturity profile, and asset-liability matching strategies.

It also mentions tables summarizing net benefit expense and funded status in the financial statements.

nodes.title: 1) Net amount recognised in the Consolidated Statement of Profit & Loss for year
nodes.summary: The section covers gratuity-related financial disclosures, including net amounts recognised in the Consolidated Statement of Profit & Loss (current service cost, interest cost, expected return on plan assets) and Other Comprehensive Income (actuarial gains/losses, return on plan assets excluding net interest). It details the net amount recognised in the Consolidated Balance Sheet, with present value of defined benefit obligation, fair value of plan assets, surplus/deficit, and reconciliations of changes in both the obligation and plan assets, along with major plan asset categories. It also presents actuarial assumptions (discount rate, salary growth, mortality, attrition), sensitivity analysis, maturity profile of gratuity obligations, and asset-liability matching strategies, including cash accumulation insurance policy, liquidity risk mitigation, interest rate risk, and assumptions for future salary increases and fund contributions.

nodes.title: 3) Net amount recognised in the Consolidated Balance Sheet
nodes.summary: The text presents notes from Adani Enterprises Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, specifically Note 51, detailing gratuity-related financial disclosures as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It includes the net amount recognised in the Consolidated Balance Sheet, showing the present value of defined benefit obligation, fair value of plan assets, and resulting surplus/deficit and net liability. It further provides a reconciliation of the change in the present value of the defined benefit obligation, covering beginning balance, acquisition adjustment, service cost, interest cost, actuarial gains/losses from demographic and financial assumptions and experience variance, benefits paid, and other adjustments. Similarly, it reconciles the change in fair value of plan assets, including beginning balance, acquisition adjustment, expected return, employer contributions, return excluding net interest, and benefits paid. Finally, it lists major categories of plan assets as a percentage of total fair value, showing insurance policy at 100% for both years.

nodes.title: Actuarial Assumptions, Sensitivity Analysis and Maturity Profile
key_items: 4) The principal actuarial assumption used are as follows:
nodes.summary: The page presents principal actuarial assumptions—discount rate, salary growth, mortality, and attrition—comparing March 31, 2025 and 2024. It includes a sensitivity analysis showing the impact of changes in these assumptions on defined benefit obligations, with rates and amounts in crore, noting assumptions may be correlated. It also provides the maturity profile of gratuity obligations, including weighted average duration and expected maturity analysis across time buckets (within 1 year, 2–5 years, 6–10 years, and more than 10 years) for both years.

nodes.title: 6) Asset - Liability Matching Strategies
nodes.summary: The text details asset-liability matching strategies for Adani Enterprises' gratuity plan, involving a yearly cash accumulation insurance policy covering gratuity outflows, with deficits funded by the company, mitigating liquidity risk but exposing the company to interest rate risk due to asset-liability duration mismatch. It also notes actuarial assumptions for future salary increases consider inflation, seniority, promotions, and market factors, and that expected fund contributions align with the current year. Additionally, it states that details of insurer-managed gratuity fund investments are unavailable.

structure.title: 52. Earnings Per Share (EPS)
structure.summary: This section covers Earnings Per Share (EPS) data for fiscal years ending March 31, 2024 and 2025, including continuing and discontinued operations, consolidated net profit attributable to owners, distribution of interest on unsecured perpetual securities, weighted average shares for basic and diluted EPS, and EPS figures for continuing, discontinued, and total operations with face value of ₹1 per share. It also references disclosures under Ind AS 111 and Ind AS 112 regarding interests in jointly controlled assets, associates, and jointly controlled entities. Jointly controlled assets details include onshore blocks (Palej and Assam) with terminated PSCs and written-off investments, and offshore blocks with participating interests, operatorship, financial shares, and status updates (gas discovery, FDP extensions, relinquishment, revised FDP approval, and early development plan review). Interest in other entities lists joint ventures and associates consolidated under the equity method with names, countries, relationship types, ownership percentages, and summarized financial position and profitability tables.

key_items: EPS in ` (face value ` 1/- each) - Basic & Diluted

It details consolidated net profit attributable to owners, distribution of interest on unsecured perpetual securities, and weighted average number of shares for basic and diluted EPS. EPS figures are provided for continuing, discontinued, and total operations, with face value of ₹1 per share. Additionally, it references disclosures under Ind AS 111 and Ind AS 112 regarding the Group's interests in jointly controlled assets, associates, and jointly controlled entities.

nodes.title: a) Jointly Controlled Assets
key_items: One of the group company's Participating Interest %
nodes.summary: The text details jointly controlled assets in oil and gas exploration. It covers two onshore blocks (Palej and Assam) awarded under NELP-VI, with PSCs terminated by the Government due to operator misrepresentation; investments were written off. It describes offshore blocks held by group companies, including participating interests, operatorship, and financial shares of assets/liabilities. For GK-OSN-2009/1, a gas discovery was made, and FDP submission timelines were extended due to COVID-19; a three-year extension is awaited. GK-OSN-2009/2 is under relinquishment. For MB/OSDSF/B9/2016, a revised FDP was approved, and development period extended to July 2025. For MB-OSN-2005/2, exploration obligations are complete, and an early development plan for the AWEL A-1 discovery is under review.

nodes.title: b) Interest in Other Entities
key_items: Name of Jointly Controlled Entities / Associates
nodes.summary: This note lists the Group's joint ventures and associates, consolidated under the equity method, providing their names, countries of incorporation (India, Singapore, Australia, UK, UAE), relationship type, and ownership percentages for March 31, 2024 and 2025. It presents summarized financial position tables—non-current and current assets, cash, non-current and current liabilities, equity, contingent liabilities, and capital commitments—and summarized profitability tables—revenue, interest income, depreciation, finance costs, profit before and after tax, tax, other comprehensive income, and total comprehensive income—for each entity, with notes on consolidated subsidiaries included in AWL Agri Business, AdaniConnex, and Sirius Digitech.

structure.title: 54. Recent Pronouncements
structure.summary: The text covers five notes to the consolidated financial statements: (54) recent pronouncements by MCA, including Ind AS 117 and amendments to Ind AS 116, with no significant impact; (55) the Code on Social Security, 2020, pending notification, with impact to be assessed later; (56) recommendation of a final dividend of ₹1.30 per equity share for FY 2024-25, and confirmation of dividend paid for FY 2023-24; (57) consolidation of certain subsidiaries based on unaudited financial statements in the previous year, with differences considered insignificant and adjusted in the current year; and (58) disclosures that no funds were advanced or received by the Parent, subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures incorporated in India with arrangements for ultimate beneficiaries, for both FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24.

structure.title: 59. Additional Regulatory Disclosures
structure.summary: The text presents two main regulatory disclosures: (59) statements that no benami property proceedings are pending, no group entity is a wilful defaulter, certain entities have bank borrowings secured by current assets with quarterly returns matching books (some exempt), and no crypto/virtual currency trading occurred. (60) provides a detailed table of net assets, profit/loss, other comprehensive income, and total comprehensive income for Adani Enterprises Limited, its Indian and foreign subsidiaries, jointly controlled entities, and associates, including percentage shares and amounts in crore, with notes on consolidated entities.

structure.title: 62. Approval of Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.summary: The text covers the approval of consolidated financial statements by the board on May 1, 2025, including signatures from auditors and directors. It then presents Form AOC-1, detailing salient features of financial statements for subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures as per the Companies Act, 2013. The table includes shareholding percentage, profit/loss before and after tax, provision for tax, sales turnover, investment, total assets, liabilities, other equity, share capital, reporting currency, and period for numerous entities, mostly for FY 2024-25. It also includes notes on exchange rates and mergers, and a list of entities consolidated within certain subsidiaries.

structure.title: Form No. AOC - 1
structure.summary: The text presents Form AOC-1 disclosing salient financial features of subsidiaries, associates, and jointly controlled entities under the Companies Act, 2013. Part A lists 92 subsidiaries yet to commence operations and eight sold or liquidated during the year. Part B details associates and jointly controlled entities with financial data including investment amounts, shareholding percentages, net worth, profits/losses, and consolidation status, plus notes on significant influence and consolidated entities. A separate list names 23 associates and joint ventures yet to commence operations. The document concludes with board signatures and officer designations.

structure.title: Notice
structure.summary: This notice covers the 33rd Annual General Meeting of Adani Enterprises Limited on June 24, 2025, held via video conferencing. Under ordinary business, it includes adoption of audited financial statements for FY2024-25, declaration of dividend, and re-appointment of Mr. Rajesh S. Adani as a rotating director. Special business includes appointment of CS Ashwin Shah as Secretarial Auditor, re-appointment of Dr. Omkar Goswami as Independent Director, approval of Cost Auditors' remuneration, and approval of numerous material related party transactions for FY2025-26. It also includes a special resolution to raise up to ₹15,000 crore through issuance of equity shares or other eligible securities via various modes, including QIP, with board authorizations.

nodes.title: ORDINARY BUSINESS
nodes.summary: The text is a notice for Adani Enterprises Limited's 33rd Annual General Meeting, scheduled for June 24, 2025, at 10:30 a.m. IST via video conferencing, with the deemed venue at the registered office in Ahmedabad. It outlines the ordinary business to be transacted: adoption of audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY ended March 31, 2025, along with Board and Auditor reports; declaration of dividend on equity shares for FY 2024-25; and re-appointment of Mr. Rajesh S. Adani (DIN: 00006322), who retires by rotation, as a Director. An explanation notes that executive and non-executive directors (other than independent) retire by rotation, and Mr. Adani, a director since 1993, is eligible and recommended by the Board and Nomination and Remuneration Committee for re-appointment. The resolution is proposed as an ordinary resolution under Section 152 of the Companies Act, 2013.

nodes.title: SPECIAL BUSINESS
nodes.summary: The section covers special business for Adani Enterprises' 33rd AGM on June 24, 2025, including appointment of CS Ashwin Shah as Secretarial Auditor for five years and re-appointment of Dr. Omkar Goswami as Independent Director for a second term. It approves remuneration for Cost Auditors M/s. K V M & Co. for FY2025-26 and numerous material related party transactions for FY2025-26 with various subsidiaries, step-down subsidiaries, joint ventures, and related parties, all at arm's length and in the ordinary course of business. It also includes a special resolution to raise up to ₹15,000 crore through issuance of equity shares or other eligible securities via various modes, with detailed terms for QIP, board authorizations for execution, listing, and related matters.

nodes.title: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT
nodes.summary: The text covers two special business items for a company meeting. Item 4 proposes appointing CS Ashwin Shah as Secretarial Auditor for a first term of five years (FY 2025-26 to FY 2029-30) via Ordinary Resolution, authorizing remuneration and additional services, and empowering the Board to take necessary actions. Item 5 proposes re-appointing Dr. Omkar Goswami as an Independent Director for a second term of three years via Special Resolution.

nodes.title: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT
nodes.summary: The notice convenes Adani Enterprises' 33rd AGM on June 24, 2025, via video conferencing. Ordinary business includes adopting audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY2024-25, declaring a dividend, and re-appointing Mr. Rajesh S. Adani as a rotating director. It cites the Nomination and Remuneration Committee's recommendation based on performance evaluation and the Board's belief that his continued association benefits the Company. It explains the progressive governance practice of two-term limits for Independent Directors to ensure independence and board refreshment aligned with global ESG practices. Legal provisions under Sections 149, 160, and 164 of the Companies Act, 2013, and SEBI Listing Regulations are referenced regarding eligibility, consent, and declarations. The text confirms Dr. Goswami meets independence criteria, has no pecuniary relationship besides remuneration, and notes the resolution is open for inspection and recommended for approval, with Dr. Goswami deemed interested.

nodes.title: For Item No. 7 to 30:

Materiality thresholds are defined as transactions exceeding ₹1,000 crore or 10% of annual consolidated turnover, whichever is lower. For FY 2025-26, the Company and subsidiaries propose related party transactions expected to cross these thresholds, seeking prior member approval. The Audit Committee has reviewed and approved the transactions, subject to member approval, confirming they are at arm's length, in the ordinary course, and per the Related Party Policy. The Board recommends resolutions in items 7 to 30. Related parties cannot vote, and Mr. Gautam S. Adani, Mr. Rajesh S. Adani, Mr. Pranav V. Adani, and their relatives are deemed interested; no other directors or key managerial personnel are interested. Details per Regulation 23(4) and SEBI Circular are provided in the annexure.

It lists disclosures for GRI 2 (General Disclosures), GRI 3 (Material Topics), and various topic-specific standards: GRI 201 (Economic Performance), 204 (Procurement Practices), 205 (Anti-corruption), 206 (Anti-competitive Behavior), 207 (Tax), 302 (Energy), 303 (Water and Effluents), 305 (Emissions), 306 (Effluents and Waste), 308 (Supplier Environmental Assessment), 401 (Employment), 403 (Occupational Health and Safety), 404 (Training and Education), 405 (Diversity and Equal Opportunity), 406 (Non-discrimination), 407 (Freedom of Association and Collective Bargaining), 408 (Child Labor), 409 (Forced or Compulsory Labor), 410 (Security Practices), 411 (Rights of Indigenous Peoples), 413 (Local Communities), 414 (Supplier Social Assessment), 415 (Public Policy), 416 (Customer Health and Safety), and 418 (Customer Privacy). Each disclosure is mapped to specific page numbers in the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: UNGC Index
structure.summary: The text is an UNGC Index from Adani Enterprises Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25. It maps the ten UN Global Compact principles to relevant report sections and page numbers. Principles 1-2 cover human rights and labor relations, including freedom of association, forced labor, child labor, and discrimination. Principles 3-4 address environmental challenges, responsibility, and eco-friendly technologies. Principle 5 focuses on anti-corruption. The sections listed span human rights, labor relations, diversity, equity and inclusion, ESG excellence, climate risk management, emissions, energy, water stewardship, waste management, biodiversity, and anti-bribery/anti-corruption, with corresponding page ranges from 59 to 734.

structure.title: Abbreviations
structure.summary: The text is an abbreviations and full forms list from Adani Enterprises Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25. It covers corporate, ESG, and financial acronyms across sectors like airports, energy, mining, logistics, and social initiatives. Included are organizational names, regulatory bodies, technical terms (e.g., 5G, CCUS, HVDC), sustainability frameworks (ESG, GRI, CDP), financial metrics (CAGR, CAPEX), and safety/HR terms (LTIFR, DEI). The list spans statutory reports, financial statements, and strategic reviews, providing definitions for diverse abbreviations used throughout the report, from ACI to PVC, without omitting any category of content.

structure.title: Full Forms
structure.summary: This text is a portfolio overview comprising a corporate strategic review and ESG overview, followed by a comprehensive abbreviations list with full forms. It covers financial, operational, regulatory, and sustainability terms across sectors like LNG, logistics, mining, renewables, and aviation. The list includes organizational abbreviations (e.g., SEBI, UNGC, NCERT), technical terms (e.g., LTIFR, MTPA, NOx, SOx), sustainability frameworks (e.g., TCFD, TNFD, SBTi), business metrics (e.g., MAU, PUE, SROI), and Indian government schemes (e.g., PM-KUSUM, PLI, NAPS). It also defines safety, health, and environmental terms (e.g., ZLD, ZWL, ODS), financial instruments (e.g., NCD, QIP), and various project and technology acronyms, concluding with a page number.
